chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The owned slave, when he flees and does not exit from his city, does not constitute as having absconded.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of an absconding slave (abiq) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of 'ruquq' by distinguishing between a simple escape and the specific legal category of 'abiq' (fugitive slave), ruling that remaining within the same 'misr' (city or administrative district) prevents the slave from acquiring this status. This distinction is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it affects the master's rights and the slave's obligations, reflecting the nuanced understanding of urban boundaries in classical Islamic law. The ruling underscores the principle that legal classifications depend on precise geographical and social contexts rather than mere physical absence.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The owned slave, when he flees and does not exit from his city, does not constitute as having absconded’.
